segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The prophet Amos carried a warning from the Lord —

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: not about food, but about something people would miss even more.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: A day would come when God's voice would seem far away — not because He stopped speaking, but because people stopped being able to hear.

segments.speaker: god
segments.text: Behold, the days come, saith the Lord GOD, that I will send a famine in the land, not a famine of bread, nor a thirst for water, but of hearing the words of the LORD:

segments.speaker: god
segments.text: And they shall wander from sea to sea, and from the north even to the east, they shall run to and fro to seek the word of the LORD, and shall not find it.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The deepest hunger isn't in the stomach. It's the ache of a soul that can't find a word from God.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: It was to listen while His voice could still be heard.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When His word is near, don't let it pass. Listen now — the famine is the silence we choose.
